home.tagline: A free open-source repository manager that proxies and caches upstream sources.
home.intro: RepoMan is built as a lightweight, modern alternative to commercial and limited Community editions for running a local cache of software dependencies and artifacts.

status.title: Early development
status.text: The API, configuration format and internal architecture may change before the first stable release. The project is not yet recommended for production use.

why.title: Why RepoMan?
why.text: Developers, servers and CI/CD systems download the same data from external sources over and over again. RepoMan sits between clients and external repositories: on the first request it fetches an artifact from upstream and stores it locally, subsequent requests are served from the cache.

benefits.availability: depend less on the availability of external services
benefits.single: use a single proxy/cache inside your infrastructure

free.title: Free, no artificial limits
free.text: No limits on the number of components, users or requests.

proxy.title: Proxy & Cache
proxy.text: Automatic caching of artifacts from upstream repositories.

formats.title: Multiple formats
formats.text: A single access point for different package managers.

openSource.title: Open Source
openSource.text: Source code is distributed under the Apache 2.0 license.

linux.title: Linux
linux.text: Target platform; development is possible on macOS and Windows (via Docker).

api.title: API-first
api.text: All configuration via REST API and Web UI, easy to automate (Ansible, Terraform, curl).

formats.title: Planned formats
formats.raw: Arbitrary HTTP files and binary artifacts

principle.title: Core principle
principle.text: RepoMan does not aim to be a large Software Supply Chain platform. The project's goal is simple:
principle.quote: One local service for fast and reliable caching of software dependencies.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.text: The requested page does not exist.

ldap.title: Active Directory / LDAP
ldap.caCertificateHint: Root certificate of your CA. If empty, system CAs are used. The server name must match the certificate.
ldap.bindPasswordSaved: Password is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
ldap.userBaseDnHint: Any active user in this subtree can sign in, e.g. DC=example,DC=com or OU=Users,DC=example,DC=com
ldap.userFilterHint: Optional. For example, allow sign-in only for members of a group (nested groups included).
ldap.maxBlockRatioHint: Synchronization is aborted if more than this share of users would be blocked

warnings.plain: Passwords of users and of the service account are sent over the network in clear text. Use only in an isolated network. Domain controllers that require LDAP signing (the default in Windows Server 2025) reject such connections.
warnings.noVerify: Traffic is encrypted but not protected against server impersonation (MITM): an attacker in the network can capture passwords of users and of the service account. Providing the CA certificate is recommended.

test.userNotFound: The test user was not found in the Base DN with the filter applied.

mappings.title: Group to role mapping
mappings.description: Group membership includes nested groups and the primary group. Groups affect only roles, not whether a user can sign in.

sync.title: User synchronization
sync.description: Updates profiles and roles of domain users, blocks users disabled in AD or no longer in the Base DN / filter.
